sections.overview: Fufius striatipes is a Brazilian mygalomorph spider currently placed in the family Rhytidicolidae; it was first described as Metriura striatipes.
sections.identification: The described male holotype measured 12.34 mm; its legs bear one or two dark stripes, and erect setae occur just before the fovea.
sections.habitat: Type specimens came from Tarumã Mirín, Amazonas, in a seasonally flooded igapó; authors cautioned that tree-climbing may have been an escape from rising water.
sections.diet: The taxonomic sources consulted do not report prey or a species-specific diet.
sections.behavior: Field behavior has not been summarized in the available species record; habits of other mygalomorphs should not be assumed for it.
sections.reproduction: The sources identify a male type specimen but do not document courtship, egg sacs, clutch size or breeding season.
sections.ecology: The original description compared Metriura, now synonymized with Fufius, with Linothele and considered them related but distinct.
sections.conservation: No population estimate or conservation assessment is provided in the consulted catalog and original description.
